context_engagements.note: Friendship, recorded without a connection line. Quoted whole.

sources.quote: My dear good Friend, I am installed here in a little inn by the sea. It is very nice, and there is no one in the whole hotel, so I am quite alone. I am still filled with wonder at the beauty of the world, and with gratitude to God for still considering me worthy to enjoy it, or perhaps I should say making me worthy of such a privilege. Do write to me, and tell me all about yourself, and your artistic plans. Have you any plays going? I know you are reciting, and envy those who hear that wonderful rich voice of yours that Browning, and indeed all poets, used to admire so much, and can watch your lithe panther-like grace of movement, and become dominated by the exquisite tyranny of your personality. However, I think of you every day, and the sea-birds, whom the wind here blows about like white flowers, seem aware of the fact, and are, apparently, quite indignant about it, if screaming counts as a sign! Send me a photograph of yourself, if you can. I want to look at your shadow: and please like and store as a secret my new name. Your affectionate friend
sources.context: Wilde to Mrs Bernard Beere, [circa 2 June 1897], Hôtel de la Plage, Berneval-sur-Mer (MS Yale) - quoted whole, and signed SEBASTIAN MELMOTH. A fortnight out of prison. The Browning who admired her voice is Robert Browning. 'Please like and store as a secret my new name' is the alias being entrusted to her, which is the same discretion machinery visible in the Dieppe letter to Ada Leverson where Ross and Turner travelled under each other's names.
sources.speaker: Oscar Wilde
sources.supports: One of the first friends written to after prison, and the alias entrusted to her.
sources.provenance: Repo PDF page 925; printed folio 875 confirmed on the rendered page image, read 2026-08-06.

name: Mrs Bernard Beere
bio: Actress, and one of Wilde's oldest theatrical friends - she created Mrs Arbuthnot in A Woman of No Importance. Nine of Wilde's letters to her survive, running from 1880 to 1897. The last of them was written from Berneval a fortnight after he came out of prison, and he signed it with his new name and asked her to keep it a secret.
bio_note: Added 2026-08-06. **SHE WAS NOT ON ANY FLAGGED LIST.** She is here because the folio was read whole rather than mined for Dalhousie Young, the name that sent me to it - which is the entire argument for the page being the unit of reading. NO CONNECTION LINE: the register is long affectionate friendship between a writer and an actress, and nothing states or implies more. NINE LETTERS at printed 152, 161, 330, 416, 590, 592, 631, 846 and 875; ONE read at the page (2026-08-06). THE LETTER BELOW IS A POST-PRISON ONE and belongs with the small group of people who were written to as friends that summer - [[leverson]], [[laurence-housman]], [[blacker]], [[dalhousie-young]].
